Step 1 (page 32): the first piece of the model, a black 2x6 plate with 4 studs on its side (b1). It is the base piece, so it rests on nothing and has no joins.

Step 2 (page 33): a black 1x4 plate (b2) is added at the end of b1, forming an L shape. The drawing does not show clearly which studs it clutches, so I recorded it as resting on b1 with no ports named.
Step 3 (page 33): a black 2x8 plate (b3, shown 1:1) is placed on top of b1 and b2. It rests on both and extends past b1.
The edge ports are left null because the exact stud positions can't be read from the isometric drawings.
Step 4 (page 34): a tan 2x10 plate (b4) is laid over the black plates b3 and b1, and its right end overhangs b3. A black 1x4 plate (b5) is then dropped onto the back row of b4.

Step 5 (page 34): a black 2x8 plate (b6) and a black 2x2 plate (b7) are added. The drawing seems to show the model from a different angle, and the arrow for the 2x2 points up at the underside. I read b6 as clutching b4 and b7 as clutching b3 from below. The exact contact pieces are uncertain, and the 2x2 colour is read as black because the list has only one black 2x2 plate.
The edge ports are left null because the exact stud positions can't be read from the drawings.

Step 6 (page 35): a black 2x4 plate (b8) and a black 1x4 plate (b9) are added. The page shows only the finished result with no arrows, so where they go is a best guess. I read b8 as clutching b4 and b3, and b9 as clutching b4 and b6.
The edge ports are left null because the exact stud positions can't be read from the drawing.

Step 7 (page 36): the callout shows a black 1x4 plate (b11) pressed onto one long edge of a black 2x4 plate (b10). That pair is then placed on the raised 2x4 plate at the back of the model, which I read as b8 from step 6.
I assumed the 2x4 in this step is the second black 2x4 plate on the parts list.
The edge ports are left null because the exact stud positions can't be read from the drawing.

Step 8 (page 37): a second black 2x6 plate with 4 side studs (b12) is added at the front right of the model, in the same bottom layer as b1. Its side studs face the front. I read it as clutching the underside of the tan plate b4, so b4 sits on b12, but this is a best guess from the drawing.
The edge ports are left null because the exact stud positions can't be read from the drawing.

Step 9 (page 38): a black 1x10 plate (b14) and a black 1x2 plate (b13) are added. The drawing shows the 1x10 already in place along the right side of the model, so I read it as clutching both b4 and b6. The 1x2 is shown dropping onto the right black section next to the end of the tan plate, so I read it as resting on b6.
The 1x10 placement is a best guess, because the callout shows it only as a piece to add.
The edge ports are left null because the exact stud positions can't be read from the drawing.

Step 10 (page 39): a black 2x8 plate (b15, shown 1:1) is added at the right end of the model, extending the long strip further right. I read it as overlapping and clutching b6 and b14, but the drawing shows only the finished result, so this is a best guess.
The edge ports are left null because the exact stud positions can't be read from the drawing.

Step 11 (page 40): a black 2x10 plate (b16, shown 1:1) is laid along the long right-hand strip. I read it as covering and clutching b6, b13, b14 and b15, but the drawing shows only the finished result, so this is a best guess.
The edge ports are left null because the exact stud positions can't be read from the drawing.
Step 12 (page 41): a black 1x10 plate (b17) and a black 2x6 plate with 4 side studs (b18) are added. The 1x10 runs along the back edge of the right-hand strip, so I read it as clutching b16 and b15.
I read b18 as joining the underside of b16 at the front, with its side studs facing outward. That matches how b12 was placed, but it is a best guess.
The edge ports are left null because the exact stud positions can't be read from the drawing.

Step 13 (page 42): a black 2x8 plate (b19, shown 1:1) is added toward the right end of the long strip. I read it as clutching b16 and b15, but the drawing shows only the finished result, so this is a best guess.
The edge ports are left null because the exact stud positions can't be read from the drawing.

Step 14 (page 43): a fourth black 2x6 plate with 4 side studs (b20) is added at the front right, with its side studs facing the front. As with b12 and b18, I read it as clutching the underside of the plate above it, here b19. That is a best guess from the drawing.
The edge ports are left null because the exact stud positions can't be read from the drawing.

Step 15 (page 44): the second tan 2x10 plate (b21) is laid at the right end of the model, overhanging the end. It mirrors the tan plate b4 at the left end. I read it as resting on b19 and b20, but the drawing shows only the finished result, so this is a best guess.
The edge ports are left null because the exact stud positions can't be read from the drawing.

Step 16 (page 45): the fifth and last black 2x6 plate with 4 side studs (b22) is added at the far right end, mirroring b1 at the left end. As with b12, b18 and b20, I read it as clutching the underside of the plate above it, here the tan plate b21. That is a best guess from the drawing.
The edge ports are left null because the exact stud positions can't be read from the drawing.

Step 17 (page 46): three black 1x2 plates (b23, b24, b25) are pushed up from below into the gaps between the side-stud plates along the front. The three arrows point up and to the right, and the pieces are not shown installed. I read them as clutching the undersides of b16, b19 and b21, but that is a best guess.
The callout also lists one black 1x4 plate (b26), but the page does not show where it goes. I guessed it clutches b16, so its placement is uncertain.
The edge ports are left null because the exact stud positions can't be read from the drawing.

Step 18 (page 47): a black 1x8 tile (b27) is attached to the front of the model at the left end, on the side studs of b1. The callout shows a plain long tile, so I used the plain lego-4162 rather than the 'Berlin' print tile, which is probably added in a later step.
The tile is shown only at the left end, and its full length is not visible in the drawing. It may also reach the side studs of b12, b18, b20 or b22, but I recorded only the join to b1.
The edge ports are left null because the exact stud positions can't be read from the drawing.

Step 19 (page 48): the box labelled 2x on the page shows two black plates, which I recorded as 1x2 plates (b28, b29) joined end to end. The 'Berlin' print tile (b30) goes on top of them. The finished sign is placed along the front of the model, above the front row of the tan plate b4.

The plate size is a guess, because the callout shows two plates that together match the length of the tile. They would be 1x4 plates, but the parts list has more 1x2 black plates than 1x4 plates left over, and the drawing is too small to tell.
I recorded the sign as resting on b4. It may also touch the tile b27 from step 18 or the studs of b1, but the drawing does not show that clearly.
The edge ports are left null because the exact stud positions can't be read from the drawing.
Step 20 (page 49): one black 1x3 tile (b31) and two long black tiles (b32, b33) are added to cover the front of the base. The long tiles are recorded as 1x8 tiles with groove.

The parts list has only two plain black 1x8 tiles. The tile b27 from step 18 plus b32 and b33 makes three, so b27 may actually have been a different tile, such as a 1x4 tile. I could not tell from the drawing and left b27 unchanged.
I read the tiles as clutching the side studs of the 87609 plates: b31 on b1, b32 on b12 and b18, b33 on b20 and b22. The drawing shows only the finished result, so this is a best guess.
The edge ports are left null because the exact stud positions can't be read from the drawing.

The page shows only the finished result, with no arrows. The grey pieces appear at the back-left of the model, around the raised 2x4 area (b10/b11) and the left end of the tan plate b4, with tiles at the left edge. All the 'rests_on' joins here are best guesses from the drawing.
The edge ports are left null because the exact stud positions can't be read from the drawing.

The page shows only the finished result with no arrows. I recorded all eight pieces as clutching b16, which is a best guess. Some may also clutch b13, b14, b6 or the grey pieces from step 21.
The edge ports are left null because the exact stud positions can't be read from the drawing.

I read both pieces as clutching b16, since the drawing shows them over the black 2x10 plate, but this is a best guess.

The page shows only the finished result with no arrows, so the placement is a best guess. I recorded b50 as clutching b16 and the 1x1 plate b49 from step 23, and the other pieces as clutching b16.

I read both panels as clutching the tan plate b4. The grey tiles from step 21 at the left end may also be part of the contact, but the drawing does not show it clearly.

Step 43 (page 76): six tan round 1x1 plates are added on the studs along the top of the fence b114. The callout shows two stacks of two plates, each placed on a fence stud, as the two arrows point. Which fence stud gets which stack is a guess. The drawing shows two raised stacks side by side near the middle of the fence.
The edge ports on the plates are left null, and the fence stud numbers are best guesses.
Step 44 (page 77): four dark bluish gray 1x1 cheese slopes (b121 to b124) are placed on top of the tan round plates on the fence. Together they form the sloped pediment roof of the Reichstag portico.
I read each slope as sitting on one plate stack: b121 on b116, b122 on b118, b123 on b119 and b124 on b120. This is a best guess, since the page shows only the finished result with no arrows.
The edge ports are left null because the exact stud positions can't be read from the drawing.

Step 45 (page 78): the tan curved 4x1 brick (b125) is placed at the front of the Reichstag, in front of the columns. It forms the curved front steps of the portico, and is the only tan curved brick in the parts list.
I read it as clutching the tan corner plates b94 and b95 at the front. The page shows only the finished result with no arrows, so this is a best guess.
The edge ports are left null because the exact stud positions can't be read from the drawing.

Page 79 starts a second small tan building, the same as the one on pages 57 to 60 (see the picture at the top of the page). It is shown being built from scratch, so I recorded it as new pieces b126 onward.
Step 1: a tan 1x4 brick (b126) goes on a light bluish gray 2x4 plate (b127). This is the fifth and last light bluish gray 2x4 plate in the parts list.
Step 2: a tan 1x2 tile (b128), a tan 1x2 brick with 2 side studs (b129, drawn with two round side studs) and a tan 1x2 brick with groove (b130) are added.

Correction to the first building: comparing the two step 2 callouts, the piece with two round side studs is the tan 1x2 side-stud brick (lego-11211), and the other is a plain tan 1x2 brick with groove (lego-4216). So in the first building, b71 and b72 were probably the wrong way round: b71 should have been lego-11211 and b72 lego-4216. The part counts agree, since the list has only two 11211 bricks, and so does the 1x2 brick that I called b81, which is likely lego-4216 too. I can't change earlier entries, so I am flagging it here.
The tan 1x1 headlight bricks (lego-4070) are the small side-stud pieces in step 7 of each building, four in total.
The placements follow the first building.

Page 80, step 3: a tan 2x2 plate (b131) and two tan grille tiles (b132, b133) are added to the second tan building. As on page 58, sub-step 2 shows a grille tile lowered onto another grille-looking piece. I recorded b133 as only touching b132, and b132 as sitting on the 1x4 brick b126.
Page 80, step 4: two tan 1x2 bricks with groove (b134, b135) are stacked and placed on top of the model. I read the stack as resting on the 2x2 plate b131.
In this copy the order of steps differs a little from the first building, and the model drawings are partly hidden, so most placements are best guesses.
The edge ports are left null because the exact stud positions can't be read from the drawing.

Page 81, step 5: two dark bluish gray 2x2 plates (b136, b137) are placed on top of the second tan building. These are the last two of the four dark bluish gray 2x2 plates in the parts list. One is shown already placed over the grille side, as in the first building.

Page 81, step 6: a dark bluish gray 1x2 tile (b138) goes on one plate, and a tan 1x2 brick (b139) on the other. Following my correction on page 79, I recorded the tan brick as the groove brick lego-4216, since the 2-stud side brick is already used up.
Which pieces are underneath is read from the drawings and is a best guess.
The edge ports are left null because the exact stud positions can't be read from the drawing.
Page 82 finishes the second tan building the same way as page 60 did for the first.
Step 7: two tan headlight bricks (b141, b142) go on the tan brick b139, with a tan round 2x2 plate (b140) on top. Two tan round 1x1 plates (b143, b144) are also added on the dark bluish gray plates.
Step 8: a dark bluish gray 2x2 jumper plate (b146) goes on top and a dark bluish gray 1x1 tile (b145) on its centre stud.
Placements follow the first building and are best guesses, since the drawings do not show every contact.
Step 46 (page 83): no new pieces. The second finished tan building (pages 79 to 82) is attached to the base on the right of the Reichstag, mirroring the first tan building at its left.
I recorded its bottom plate b127 as clutching the tan plate b4 and the grey plate b35. The drawing doesn't show which base pieces are directly under it, so this is a best guess.
The edge ports are left null because the exact stud positions can't be read from the drawing.
Step 47 (page 84): a small round tower is built as a separate unit and then attached to the base.

Sub-step 1: two tan 2x2 plates (b147, b148) are stacked. Sub-step 2: a tan round 2x2 grill brick (b149) goes on top. Sub-step 3: a dark bluish gray round 2x2 jumper plate (b150) is the roof. The finished tower is placed on the base just to the right of the second tan building.
I recorded the tower's bottom plate b148 as clutching the black plate b16. The drawing doesn't show which base pieces are directly under it, so this is a best guess.
The edge ports are left null because the exact stud positions can't be read from the drawing.
Step 48 (page 85): the Berlin TV tower shaft is built from six round 1x1 plates, three tan and three white, stacked on the stud of the round jumper plate b150.
The three sub-steps show the order from the bottom up: tan, white, tan, white, tan, white. That gives three of each colour, matching the 3x and 3x in the callout.
The edge ports are left null because the exact stud positions can't be read from the drawing.
Step 49 (page 86): the pearl gold trophy statuette (b157) is pushed onto the top stud of the stacked round plate column, as the arrow shows. It is the Victoria statue on top of the Victory Column.
The page also has a fun-fact box about 285 steps to the Victory Column platform, which adds no pieces.
Page 87 starts a third sub-model: the curved black Deutsche Bahn tower with a red top (see the picture at the top of the page). It is built separately and attached to the base later.

Step 1: a black Technic brick 1x2 with a pin hole (b159) goes on a 2x2 plate (b158). The plate looks lighter in the drawing, so its colour is uncertain. Black 2x2 plate lego-3022 and the inverted tile lego-11203 are the only black 2x2 candidates, and I chose the plate.
Step 2: two black 1x1 bricks with a stud on one side (b160, b161) go on the studs of the Technic brick, with their side studs facing outward.
The edge ports are left null because the exact stud positions can't be read from the drawing.
Page 88, step 3: the model is turned over. No new pieces.

Page 88, step 4: two black 1x2 plates are stacked (b162 on b163), and two black 1x1 side-stud bricks (b164, b165) go on top of them. I read the bottom plate b163 as snapping onto the side studs of b160 and b161, as the arrow points sideways at the model.
The drawing doesn't make clear which plate sits against the model, so these joins are best guesses.
The edge ports on the other ends are left null because the exact stud positions can't be read from the drawing.

Page 89, steps 5 and 6: the same four-piece unit as step 4 is built twice more to grow the black tower upward. Each unit is two black 1x2 plates stacked with two black 1x1 side-stud bricks on top, and is placed on the top of the stack below.
Step 5 gives b166 to b169 and step 6 gives b170 to b173. I read each new bottom plate as clutching the two side-stud bricks of the unit under it, which is a best guess.
The edge ports are left null because the exact stud positions can't be read from the drawing.
Page 90, step 7: the same unit as before (two black 1x2 plates stacked, two black side-stud bricks on top) is added to the top of the tower (b174 to b177).

Page 90, step 8: a long black plate (b178) is pressed onto the column of side studs on the face of the tower, and a black 1x2 tile (b179) closes the top. I recorded the long plate as a black 2x10 plate, but the callout is small and it could be a 1x10 plate (lego-4477), since the tower face shows one column of ten side studs.
I recorded b178 as joined to one side-stud brick per tower unit, as a best guess. It probably clutches more studs than that.
The black 1x2 plate count is now at or past what the parts list holds, so one of the earlier 1x2 plates may be another type. This could not be settled from the drawings.
The edge ports are left null because the exact stud positions can't be read from the drawing.

Page 91, step 9: two black 1x10 plates are stacked (b181 on b180). Five black 1x2 slopes (b182 to b186) go along the top, making a sloped strip. The finished strip is then pressed onto the studded face of the tower, as the arrow shows. I read the callout slopes as the 1x2 slope lego-85984 because five of them span ten studs.
I recorded b180 as clutching the long plate b178 on the tower face, which is a best guess.

Page 92, step 10 begins a separate small assembly, the red-tipped roof strip of the tower (see the picture at the top of the page). The callout lists a black 1x2 plate, a 1x2 tile, two 1x2 slopes, a 1x4 tile, a 1x4 plate, a 1x10 plate and a red cheese slope.

Only sub-steps 1 and 2 are drawn on this page. In sub-step 1 a black 1x4 plate (b188) is pressed onto one end of a black 1x10 plate (b187). In sub-step 2 a black 1x2 plate (b189) is added beside it on the same 1x10 plate.
The tiles, slopes and red cheese slope from the callout are not shown placed yet, so I left them for the next page.
The edge ports are left null because the exact stud positions can't be read from the drawing.

Page 93, step 10 continued: sub-step 3 puts the red cheese slope (b190) on the end of the black strip. Sub-step 4 adds the two black 1x2 slopes (b191, b192), a black 1x2 tile (b193) and a black 1x4 tile (b194), which finish the sloped roof with a red tip. These match the remaining pieces in the step 10 callout on page 92.

The drawings show the finished result of each sub-step with no arrows, so the exact stud positions of the slopes and tiles are best guesses. The 1x4 tile may be lego-2431 in black, the one the parts list has.
The edge ports are left null because the exact stud positions can't be read from the drawing.

Page 94, step 10 (sub-step 5): no new pieces. The finished red-tipped roof strip (b187 with the plates, slopes and tiles from page 93) is pressed onto the studded face of the tower, next to the strip of slopes added on page 91.
I recorded the join as b187 clutching the long plate b178 on the tower face. It may also touch other tower pieces, but the drawing doesn't show which.
The edge ports are left null because the exact stud positions can't be read from the drawing.

Page 95, steps 11 and 12: five black curved 4x1 bricks are added in each step (b195 to b199, then b200 to b204). Together they cover the studded face of the tower in ten curved bands, which leaves ten black curved bricks and the parts list has exactly ten.

Step 11 covers the lower half of the studs and step 12 covers the rest. Each brick is recorded as clutching the long plate b178 whose studs it covers. The drawings do not show which exact studs each brick covers, so these joins are best guesses.
The edge ports are left null because the exact stud positions can't be read from the drawing.
Step 50 (page 96): no new pieces. The finished curved black Deutsche Bahn tower with its red tip is attached to the base, to the right of the round TV tower.
I recorded its bottom plate b158 as clutching the black plate b16. The drawing doesn't show which base pieces are directly under it, so this is a best guess.
The edge ports are left null because the exact stud positions can't be read from the drawing.

Page 97 starts the white Berlin TV Tower, the fourth sub-model (see the picture at the top of the page). The callout lists one 6L bar, 2x small Technic pins (the 1/2 pins), 4x black Technic pins, 5x white round pin connectors and one white 2x2x2 cone. The page also has a fun-fact box about the elevators.

Steps 1 to 3 build the shaft by alternating black pins and white round connectors. In step 1 a connector (b208) is pushed onto a pin (b205). In step 2 another pin (b206) and connector (b209) are added, and in step 3 pin b207 and connector b210. The drawing shows one pin at the bottom end of the first connector, which probably goes into the cone later.
The page shows only 3 of the 4 black pins and 3 of the 5 connectors, so the rest are on the next page. I used pin.1 and pin.2 as the two ends of a connector, following the catalogue's port names.
I'm not sure that a pin goes into each connector in the order I gave, because the drawings are small.

Page 98, steps 4 to 6: the white shaft grows by adding a pin and a connector each time. Step 4 adds a fourth black pin (b211) and a fourth connector (b212). Step 5 adds a pin (b213) and the fifth connector (b214). Step 6 adds a pin (b215) on top of the five-connector stack.

The drawings show the pins in steps 5 and 6 looking slightly different, and the parts list has only four black full pins plus two 1/2 pins. So I recorded b213 and b215 as the two light bluish gray 1/2 pins (lego-4274), which is a best guess. That means the bottom pin b205 from page 97 and the pins b206, b207 and b211 account for the four black pins.
The last pin (b215) probably holds the 6L bar, which comes in the next steps.

Page 99, step 7: the light bluish gray 6L bar (b216) is pushed up through the white cone (b217), and the bar-and-cone pair is attached to the bottom of the white pin-and-connector shaft. The cone then forms the base of the TV tower.
I recorded the bar's top end as pushed into the bottom connector b208, and the cone as sitting on the bar's stop ring. The drawing is small, so these joins are best guesses.
The parts list has two 6L bars, white and light bluish gray, and the callout drawing is grey, so I chose light bluish gray. The white one may be used for the antenna later.
Page 100 (step 8): no new pieces. The finished white TV tower is attached to the base, right of the Deutsche Bahn tower, with its cone b217 sitting on the base.
I recorded the cone as clutching the black plate b16. The drawing doesn't show which base pieces are directly under it, so this is a best guess.
The edge ports are left null because the exact stud positions can't be read from the drawing.
Page 101 starts the fifth sub-model, the observation sphere and mast of the TV tower (see the picture at the top of the page).

Step 1: two white 2x2 inverted dishes (b219, b220) are slid down a white 6L bar (b218). Step 2: a light bluish gray bush (b221) and a light bluish gray 2x2 dish (b222) are slid down the bar after them. The stack so far is two white dishes, then the bush, then the grey dish.
I read the dishes as threaded onto the bar through their centre holes and held in place on it. The catalogue lists the dish with anti-stud ports only, so I joined them to the bar with bar.1.
The grey dish b222 is recorded as the light bluish gray lego-4740 and the white dishes as the white ones. The callout drawings are small.

Page 102, step 3: a dark bluish gray 3x3 inverted dish (b223) is slid down the bar above the 2x2 dishes. Step 4: a metallic silver 3x3 dish (b224) goes on top of it. The silver dish looks pinkish in the drawing, and the parts list has two silver 3x3 dishes and two dark bluish gray ones.
The dishes are held on the white bar b218 and rest against the dish below, so I recorded them as joined to the bar and in contact with each other.

Page 103, step 5: the second metallic silver 3x3 dish (b225) is slid onto the bar. Step 6: the second dark bluish gray 3x3 dish (b226) and the second light bluish gray 2x2 dish (b227) are added. They finish the layered observation sphere. I read the small callout dish in step 6 as light bluish gray, because the parts list has two of those.
The dishes are held on the white bar b218 and rest against the dish below, so I recorded them as joined to the bar and in contact with each other.

Step 52 (page 104): no new pieces. The finished layered sphere (built on pages 101 to 103) is pushed onto the top of the white TV tower shaft. The sphere's bar b218 goes into the pin b215 at the top of the shaft.
I recorded the join as b218 inserted into b215. The arrow shows the sphere being lowered from above, but the bar's end is hidden inside the sphere.

Step 53 (page 105): the third printed panel, the sand green and dark green arrows panel (b228), is placed on the front edge of the tan plate b21 at the right end of the base, as the arrow shows. The first two printed panels went at the left end on page 56.
I read it as clutching the tan plate b21, which is a best guess.
The edge ports are left null because the exact stud positions can't be read from the drawing.

Step 54 (page 106): twelve small 'trees' are built, each two tan round 1x1 plates stacked. That uses the 24 plates in the callout. Six trees go in a cluster toward the left of the right-hand plate area and six in a cluster at the very right end, as the two arrows show.

I wrote the tree once as a repeat with 12 copies. The first six are recorded on the light bluish gray 2x2 plate b56 and the last six on the 2x2 plate b61. The drawings do not show the exact studs under each tree, so which base plate each cluster rests on is a best guess.
Each tree's bottom plate is recorded with ports stud.1.1 / anti.1.1 on the round plates, following the catalogue's port names.

Step 55 (page 107): four sand green cheese slopes (b253 to b256) are added on top of the tan tree stacks as green foliage. Two slopes sit on the left cluster of trees and two on the right cluster, as the finished image shows.

I recorded each slope on the top plate of a different tree, using the repeat copy ids tree1.top, tree2.top, tree7.top and tree8.top. The page shows only the finished result with no arrows, so which trees get the slopes is a best guess.
Step 56 (page 108): four more sand green cheese slopes (b257 to b260) are added on top of other tan tree stacks, again two per cluster, so each cluster now has a green roof of paired slopes.
I recorded them on tree3, tree4, tree9 and tree10. The page shows only the finished result with no arrows, so which trees get slopes is a best guess.
Step 57 (page 109): two sand green 1x2 tiles (b261, b262) are added, one on each tree cluster, to fill in the green foliage between the slopes.

I read each tile as spanning the tops of two trees (tree5 and tree6 on the left cluster, tree11 and tree12 on the right). The page shows only the finished result with no arrows, so this is a best guess.

Step 58 (page 110): two tan 1x4x2 spindled fences (b263, b264) are placed side by side on the tan plate b21 at the right end of the base, between the two tree clusters. They are the columns of the Brandenburg Gate. These are the second and third of the three fences in the parts list.
I recorded both as clutching the tan plate b21. The page shows only the finished result with no arrows, so this is a best guess.
The edge ports are left null because the exact stud positions can't be read from the drawing.
Step 59 (page 111): eight tan round 1x1 plates (b265 to b272) are put on the eight top studs of the two fences b263 and b264. The page also has a fun-fact box about the Brandenburg Gate.
I assigned them four to each fence in order along the studs, which matches the finished image where all eight studs are covered.

Step 60 (page 112): three sand green 1x2 tiles (b273 to b275) are added on top of the round plates on the gate. They form the sloping green roof of the Brandenburg Gate with the tiles from the next step.

The page shows only the finished result with no arrows. I read each tile as covering two of the round plates, so the three tiles cover six of the eight studs. The other two studs are probably covered by the next step. This placement is a best guess.

Step 61 (page 113): the Quadriga, the chariot sculpture on top of the Brandenburg Gate, is built as a small unit and placed on the gate roof. Sub-step 1: a sand green 1x2 plate (b276). Sub-step 2: a dark bluish gray 1x2 jumper plate (b280) and two dark bluish gray vertical clip plates (b277, b278) are added. Sub-step 3: a dark bluish gray clip tile (b279) goes on the jumper's stud.

The clip plates and clip tile form the horses and chariot, but the drawings are small, so I could not see exactly where each clip goes. I recorded the clip plates as pushed onto b276, and the clip tile on the jumper stud.
I put the finished unit on the last two uncovered round plates of the gate (b271, b272), which is a best guess.
Page 114 starts the sixth sub-model, the red and white striped antenna mast for the TV tower (see the picture at the top of the page).

Step 1: a red round 1x1 plate (b282) goes on the top stud of a dark bluish gray 1x1 brick with studs on four sides (b281). Step 2: a stack of plates is built in the order red (b282), white (b283), red (b285), white (b284). The two white plates and one red plate in the step 2 callout match the stack drawn.
In the drawing the finished antenna also has a white bar through the middle, which should come in the next steps.

Page 115, step 3: three more round 1x1 plates are stacked on the antenna base, in the order red (b287), white (b286), red (b288), as the arrows show. That makes the red and white stripes. This uses all four red round plates in the parts list, including the one at the base from page 114.
Page 115, step 4: the white 1x4 antenna with flat top (b289) is pushed onto the top stud of the stripe stack. This finishes the mast.
Step 62 (page 116): no new pieces. The finished red and white antenna mast from pages 114 and 115 is pushed onto the top of the sphere, which completes the TV tower.
I recorded the mast's bottom brick b281 as attached to the end of the sphere's bar b218 and touching the top dish b227. The page doesn't show the exact join, so this is a best guess.

Step 1: a black Technic brick 1x2 with a pin hole (b159) goes on a 2x2 plate (b158). The plate looks lighter in the drawing, so its colour is uncertain. Black 2x2 plate lego-3022 and the inverted tile lego-11203 are the only black 2x2 candidates, and I chose the plate.
Step 2: two black 1x1 bricks with a stud on one side (b160, b161) go on the studs of the Technic brick, with their side studs facing outward.
The edge ports are left null because the exact stud positions can't be read from the drawing.
Page 88, step 3: the model is turned over. No new pieces.

Page 88, step 4: two black 1x2 plates are stacked (b162 on b163), and two black 1x1 side-stud bricks (b164, b165) go on top of them. I read the bottom plate b163 as snapping onto the side studs of b160 and b161, as the arrow points sideways at the model.
The drawing doesn't make clear which plate sits against the model, so these joins are best guesses.
The edge ports on the other ends are left null because the exact stud positions can't be read from the drawing.

Page 89, steps 5 and 6: the same four-piece unit as step 4 is built twice more to grow the black tower upward. Each unit is two black 1x2 plates stacked with two black 1x1 side-stud bricks on top, and is placed on the top of the stack below.
Step 5 gives b166 to b169 and step 6 gives b170 to b173. I read each new bottom plate as clutching the two side-stud bricks of the unit under it, which is a best guess.
The edge ports are left null because the exact stud positions can't be read from the drawing.
Page 90, step 7: the same unit as before (two black 1x2 plates stacked, two black side-stud bricks on top) is added to the top of the tower (b174 to b177).

Page 90, step 8: a long black plate (b178) is pressed onto the column of side studs on the face of the tower, and a black 1x2 tile (b179) closes the top. I recorded the long plate as a black 2x10 plate, but the callout is small and it could be a 1x10 plate (lego-4477), since the tower face shows one column of ten side studs.
I recorded b178 as joined to one side-stud brick per tower unit, as a best guess. It probably clutches more studs than that.
The black 1x2 plate count is now at or past what the parts list holds, so one of the earlier 1x2 plates may be another type. This could not be settled from the drawings.
The edge ports are left null because the exact stud positions can't be read from the drawing.

Page 91, step 9: two black 1x10 plates are stacked (b181 on b180). Five black 1x2 slopes (b182 to b186) go along the top, making a sloped strip. The finished strip is then pressed onto the studded face of the tower, as the arrow shows. I read the callout slopes as the 1x2 slope lego-85984 because five of them span ten studs.
I recorded b180 as clutching the long plate b178 on the tower face, which is a best guess.

Page 92, step 10 begins a separate small assembly, the red-tipped roof strip of the tower (see the picture at the top of the page). The callout lists a black 1x2 plate, a 1x2 tile, two 1x2 slopes, a 1x4 tile, a 1x4 plate, a 1x10 plate and a red cheese slope.

Only sub-steps 1 and 2 are drawn on this page. In sub-step 1 a black 1x4 plate (b188) is pressed onto one end of a black 1x10 plate (b187). In sub-step 2 a black 1x2 plate (b189) is added beside it on the same 1x10 plate.
The tiles, slopes and red cheese slope from the callout are not shown placed yet, so I left them for the next page.
The edge ports are left null because the exact stud positions can't be read from the drawing.

Page 93, step 10 continued: sub-step 3 puts the red cheese slope (b190) on the end of the black strip. Sub-step 4 adds the two black 1x2 slopes (b191, b192), a black 1x2 tile (b193) and a black 1x4 tile (b194), which finish the sloped roof with a red tip. These match the remaining pieces in the step 10 callout on page 92.

The drawings show the finished result of each sub-step with no arrows, so the exact stud positions of the slopes and tiles are best guesses. The 1x4 tile may be lego-2431 in black, the one the parts list has.
The edge ports are left null because the exact stud positions can't be read from the drawing.

Page 94, step 10 (sub-step 5): no new pieces. The finished red-tipped roof strip (b187 with the plates, slopes and tiles from page 93) is pressed onto the studded face of the tower, next to the strip of slopes added on page 91.
I recorded the join as b187 clutching the long plate b178 on the tower face. It may also touch other tower pieces, but the drawing doesn't show which.
The edge ports are left null because the exact stud positions can't be read from the drawing.

Page 95, steps 11 and 12: five black curved 4x1 bricks are added in each step (b195 to b199, then b200 to b204). Together they cover the studded face of the tower in ten curved bands, which leaves ten black curved bricks and the parts list has exactly ten.

Step 11 covers the lower half of the studs and step 12 covers the rest. Each brick is recorded as clutching the long plate b178 whose studs it covers. The drawings do not show which exact studs each brick covers, so these joins are best guesses.
The edge ports are left null because the exact stud positions can't be read from the drawing.
Step 50 (page 96): no new pieces. The finished curved black Deutsche Bahn tower with its red tip is attached to the base, to the right of the round TV tower.
I recorded its bottom plate b158 as clutching the black plate b16. The drawing doesn't show which base pieces are directly under it, so this is a best guess.
The edge ports are left null because the exact stud positions can't be read from the drawing.

Page 97 starts the white Berlin TV Tower, the fourth sub-model (see the picture at the top of the page). The callout lists one 6L bar, 2x small Technic pins (the 1/2 pins), 4x black Technic pins, 5x white round pin connectors and one white 2x2x2 cone. The page also has a fun-fact box about the elevators.

Steps 1 to 3 build the shaft by alternating black pins and white round connectors. In step 1 a connector (b208) is pushed onto a pin (b205). In step 2 another pin (b206) and connector (b209) are added, and in step 3 pin b207 and connector b210. The drawing shows one pin at the bottom end of the first connector, which probably goes into the cone later.
The page shows only 3 of the 4 black pins and 3 of the 5 connectors, so the rest are on the next page. I used pin.1 and pin.2 as the two ends of a connector, following the catalogue's port names.
I'm not sure that a pin goes into each connector in the order I gave, because the drawings are small.

Page 98, steps 4 to 6: the white shaft grows by adding a pin and a connector each time. Step 4 adds a fourth black pin (b211) and a fourth connector (b212). Step 5 adds a pin (b213) and the fifth connector (b214). Step 6 adds a pin (b215) on top of the five-connector stack.

The drawings show the pins in steps 5 and 6 looking slightly different, and the parts list has only four black full pins plus two 1/2 pins. So I recorded b213 and b215 as the two light bluish gray 1/2 pins (lego-4274), which is a best guess. That means the bottom pin b205 from page 97 and the pins b206, b207 and b211 account for the four black pins.
The last pin (b215) probably holds the 6L bar, which comes in the next steps.

Page 99, step 7: the light bluish gray 6L bar (b216) is pushed up through the white cone (b217), and the bar-and-cone pair is attached to the bottom of the white pin-and-connector shaft. The cone then forms the base of the TV tower.
I recorded the bar's top end as pushed into the bottom connector b208, and the cone as sitting on the bar's stop ring. The drawing is small, so these joins are best guesses.
The parts list has two 6L bars, white and light bluish gray, and the callout drawing is grey, so I chose light bluish gray. The white one may be used for the antenna later.
Page 100 (step 8): no new pieces. The finished white TV tower is attached to the base, right of the Deutsche Bahn tower, with its cone b217 sitting on the base.
I recorded the cone as clutching the black plate b16. The drawing doesn't show which base pieces are directly under it, so this is a best guess.
The edge ports are left null because the exact stud positions can't be read from the drawing.
Page 101 starts the fifth sub-model, the observation sphere and mast of the TV tower (see the picture at the top of the page).

Step 1: two white 2x2 inverted dishes (b219, b220) are slid down a white 6L bar (b218). Step 2: a light bluish gray bush (b221) and a light bluish gray 2x2 dish (b222) are slid down the bar after them. The stack so far is two white dishes, then the bush, then the grey dish.
I read the dishes as threaded onto the bar through their centre holes and held in place on it. The catalogue lists the dish with anti-stud ports only, so I joined them to the bar with bar.1.
The grey dish b222 is recorded as the light bluish gray lego-4740 and the white dishes as the white ones. The callout drawings are small.

Page 102, step 3: a dark bluish gray 3x3 inverted dish (b223) is slid down the bar above the 2x2 dishes. Step 4: a metallic silver 3x3 dish (b224) goes on top of it. The silver dish looks pinkish in the drawing, and the parts list has two silver 3x3 dishes and two dark bluish gray ones.
The dishes are held on the white bar b218 and rest against the dish below, so I recorded them as joined to the bar and in contact with each other.

Page 103, step 5: the second metallic silver 3x3 dish (b225) is slid onto the bar. Step 6: the second dark bluish gray 3x3 dish (b226) and the second light bluish gray 2x2 dish (b227) are added. They finish the layered observation sphere. I read the small callout dish in step 6 as light bluish gray, because the parts list has two of those.
The dishes are held on the white bar b218 and rest against the dish below, so I recorded them as joined to the bar and in contact with each other.

Step 52 (page 104): no new pieces. The finished layered sphere (built on pages 101 to 103) is pushed onto the top of the white TV tower shaft. The sphere's bar b218 goes into the pin b215 at the top of the shaft.
I recorded the join as b218 inserted into b215. The arrow shows the sphere being lowered from above, but the bar's end is hidden inside the sphere.

Step 53 (page 105): the third printed panel, the sand green and dark green arrows panel (b228), is placed on the front edge of the tan plate b21 at the right end of the base, as the arrow shows. The first two printed panels went at the left end on page 56.
I read it as clutching the tan plate b21, which is a best guess.
The edge ports are left null because the exact stud positions can't be read from the drawing.

Step 54 (page 106): twelve small 'trees' are built, each two tan round 1x1 plates stacked. That uses the 24 plates in the callout. Six trees go in a cluster toward the left of the right-hand plate area and six in a cluster at the very right end, as the two arrows show.

I wrote the tree once as a repeat with 12 copies. The first six are recorded on the light bluish gray 2x2 plate b56 and the last six on the 2x2 plate b61. The drawings do not show the exact studs under each tree, so which base plate each cluster rests on is a best guess.
Each tree's bottom plate is recorded with ports stud.1.1 / anti.1.1 on the round plates, following the catalogue's port names.

Step 55 (page 107): four sand green cheese slopes (b253 to b256) are added on top of the tan tree stacks as green foliage. Two slopes sit on the left cluster of trees and two on the right cluster, as the finished image shows.

I recorded each slope on the top plate of a different tree, using the repeat copy ids tree1.top, tree2.top, tree7.top and tree8.top. The page shows only the finished result with no arrows, so which trees get the slopes is a best guess.
Step 56 (page 108): four more sand green cheese slopes (b257 to b260) are added on top of other tan tree stacks, again two per cluster, so each cluster now has a green roof of paired slopes.
I recorded them on tree3, tree4, tree9 and tree10. The page shows only the finished result with no arrows, so which trees get slopes is a best guess.
Step 57 (page 109): two sand green 1x2 tiles (b261, b262) are added, one on each tree cluster, to fill in the green foliage between the slopes.

I read each tile as spanning the tops of two trees (tree5 and tree6 on the left cluster, tree11 and tree12 on the right). The page shows only the finished result with no arrows, so this is a best guess.

Step 58 (page 110): two tan 1x4x2 spindled fences (b263, b264) are placed side by side on the tan plate b21 at the right end of the base, between the two tree clusters. They are the columns of the Brandenburg Gate. These are the second and third of the three fences in the parts list.
I recorded both as clutching the tan plate b21. The page shows only the finished result with no arrows, so this is a best guess.
The edge ports are left null because the exact stud positions can't be read from the drawing.
Step 59 (page 111): eight tan round 1x1 plates (b265 to b272) are put on the eight top studs of the two fences b263 and b264. The page also has a fun-fact box about the Brandenburg Gate.
I assigned them four to each fence in order along the studs, which matches the finished image where all eight studs are covered.

Step 60 (page 112): three sand green 1x2 tiles (b273 to b275) are added on top of the round plates on the gate. They form the sloping green roof of the Brandenburg Gate with the tiles from the next step.

The page shows only the finished result with no arrows. I read each tile as covering two of the round plates, so the three tiles cover six of the eight studs. The other two studs are probably covered by the next step. This placement is a best guess.

Step 61 (page 113): the Quadriga, the chariot sculpture on top of the Brandenburg Gate, is built as a small unit and placed on the gate roof. Sub-step 1: a sand green 1x2 plate (b276). Sub-step 2: a dark bluish gray 1x2 jumper plate (b280) and two dark bluish gray vertical clip plates (b277, b278) are added. Sub-step 3: a dark bluish gray clip tile (b279) goes on the jumper's stud.

The clip plates and clip tile form the horses and chariot, but the drawings are small, so I could not see exactly where each clip goes. I recorded the clip plates as pushed onto b276, and the clip tile on the jumper stud.
I put the finished unit on the last two uncovered round plates of the gate (b271, b272), which is a best guess.

Step 1: a red round 1x1 plate (b282) goes on the top stud of a dark bluish gray 1x1 brick with studs on four sides (b281). Step 2: a stack of plates is built in the order red (b282), white (b283), red (b285), white (b284). The two white plates and one red plate in the step 2 callout match the stack drawn.
In the drawing the finished antenna also has a white bar through the middle, which should come in the next steps.

Page 115, step 3: three more round 1x1 plates are stacked on the antenna base, in the order red (b287), white (b286), red (b288), as the arrows show. That makes the red and white stripes. This uses all four red round plates in the parts list, including the one at the base from page 114.
Page 115, step 4: the white 1x4 antenna with flat top (b289) is pushed onto the top stud of the stripe stack. This finishes the mast.
Step 62 (page 116): no new pieces. The finished red and white antenna mast from pages 114 and 115 is pushed onto the top of the sphere, which completes the TV tower.
I recorded the mast's bottom brick b281 as attached to the end of the sphere's bar b218 and touching the top dish b227. The page doesn't show the exact join, so this is a best guess.
